claim: In LIHC patients (n=363), there is a positive correlation between the expression of NK-cell-associated genes (NCR1, KLRB1, CD160, PRF1, etc.) and PRDM1 expression.
source: Examination of 363 liver hepatocellular carcinoma (LIHC) patient samples from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) revealed a positive correlation between the expression of NK-cell-associated genes (Cursons et al., 2019) (NCR1, KLRB1, CD160, PRF1, etc.) and PRDM1 expression (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of TCGA patient data shown in Figure 1A, which displays correlation between NK gene signatures and PRDM1.

claim: LIHC patients with higher levels of NK-PRDM1 expression (above the median) have better survival outcomes compared to those with lower levels.
source: Notably, patients exhibiting higher levels of NK-PRDM1 expression (above the median) experienced better survival outcomes compared to those with lower levels of NK-PRDM1 expression (below the median; Figure 1C).
evidence: Survival analysis data from TCGA LIHC patients shown in Figure 1C demonstrates differential survival based on NK-PRDM1 expression levels.

claim: Similar positive correlations between NK-PRDM1 expression and survival were found in SKCM (n=454) and LUAD (n=497) patients.
source: Similar results were also found in skin cutaneous melanoma (SKCM, n=454) and lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD, n=497) patients (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-F).
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of additional TCGA datasets for SKCM and LUAD shown in supplementary figures.

claim: Patients in the highest quartile of NK-PRDM1 signature expression demonstrated enhanced overall survival in LUAD and SKCM patients with statistical significance.
source: Patients within the highest quartile of NK-PRDM1 signature expression demonstrated enhanced overall survival, a result that achieved statistical significance in LUAD and SKCM patients (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G-I).
evidence: Quartile-based survival analysis shown in supplementary figures demonstrates statistically significant survival differences.

claim: PRDM1 in NK cells is essential for immune surveillance in solid tumors, including liver cancer.
source: These data suggested that PRDM1 in NK cells might be essential for immune surveillance in solid tumors, including liver cancer, and prompted us to investigate the function and mechanism of PRDM1 in NK cells and ILC1 within the context of liver cancer.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the correlation and survival data presented, suggesting a functional role for PRDM1.

claim: Ncr1-Cre mice were crossed with Prdm1fl/fl mice to generate Ncr1-cre Prdm1fl/fl mice, which specifically knockout exons 6–8 of Prdm1 in NKp46-positive cells.
source: Ncr1-Cre mice were crossed with Prdm1fl/fl mice to generate Ncr1-cre Prdm1fl/fl mice, which specifically knockout exons 6–8 of Prdm1 (Shapiro-Shelef et al., 2003) in NKp46-positive cells (Figure 1D).
evidence: The experimental design and genetic strategy are described with citation to the Prdm1 floxed allele design.

claim: The expression of Prdm1 was almost undetectable in CD3-NK1.1+NKp46+ cells of Prdm1 cko mice.
source: The expression of Prdm1 was almost undetectable in CD3-NK1.1+NKp46+ cells of Prdm1 cko mice, while was similar between total splenocytes in Prdm1+/+ and Prdm1 cko mice (Figure 1, E and F) indicating successful, and specifical knockout of Prdm1 in NKp46+ cells.
evidence: RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1E and F validates the specific knockout of Prdm1 in NKp46+ cells.

claim: The percentage and absolute number of NK cells among lymphocytes was decreased in blood, lung, liver, spleen, and lymph nodes in Prdm1 cko mice compared with Prdm1+/+ mice.
source: Compared with Prdm1+/+ mice, the percentage and absolute number of NK cells (CD45+CD3-NK1.1+NKp46+) among lymphocytes was decreased in all of these tissues, whereas increased number of NK cells were observed in bone marrow (Figure 1G; Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Flow cytometry data from multiple tissues shown in Figure 1G demonstrates changes in NK cell numbers.

claim: Increased number of NK cells were observed in bone marrow of Prdm1 cko mice.
source: Compared with Prdm1+/+ mice, the percentage and absolute number of NK cells (CD45+CD3-NK1.1+NKp46+) among lymphocytes was decreased in all of these tissues, whereas increased number of NK cells were observed in bone marrow (Figure 1G; Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Flow cytometry data shows an increase in NK cells specifically in bone marrow after Prdm1 knockout.

claim: The proportion of the most mature CD11b+CD27- NK cells were significantly decreased in all analyzed tissues in Prdm1 cko mice.
source: Compared with Prdm1+/+ mice, the proportion of the most mature CD11b+CD27- NK cells were significantly decreased in all of the analyzed tissues in Prdm1 cko mice (Figure 1H; Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Flow cytometry analysis of NK cell maturation markers shown in Figure 1H demonstrates reduced mature NK cells.

claim: Stage IV (CD11b+CD27-) NK cells show higher level of effector molecules than any other stages and are considered as the most mature NK cells.
source: Stage IV (CD11b+CD27-) NK cells show higher level of effector molecules than any other stages and are considered as the most mature NK cells (Chiossone et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Chiossone et al., 2009.

claim: A significant loss of KLRG1+ cells in NK cells was observed in Prdm1 cko mice.
source: Consistent with CD11b/CD27 based maturation analysis, a significant loss of KLRG1+ cells in NK cells was observed in Prdm1 cko mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: Flow cytometry data for KLRG1 expression shown in supplementary figure confirms reduced mature NK cells.

claim: Prdm1 is required for the terminal maturation of NK cells among various tissues.
source: Together, these data confirmed that Prdm1 is required for the terminal maturation of NK cells among various tissues.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from multiple maturation marker analyses across different tissues.

claim: Prdm1 cko mice exhibited an increased percentage of cNK cells (CD49a-CD49b+) and reduced proportion of ILC1s (CD49a+CD49b-) in the liver.
source: Compared with Prdm1+/+ mice, the Prdm1 cko mice exhibited an increased percentage of cNK cells (CD49a-CD49b+) and reduced proportion of ILC1s (CD49a+CD49b-) (Figure 2A).
evidence: Flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 2A demonstrates altered proportions of liver group 1 ILC subsets.

claim: The absolute number of both cNK cells and ILC1s were decreased in Prdm1 cko mice, with a more robust reduction in ILC1s.
source: Of note, the absolute number of both cNK cells and ILC1s were decreased in Prdm1 cko mice, with a more robustly reduction in ILC1s (Figure 2A), which underscored the crucial role of Prdm1 in maintaining the quantity of both liver cNK cells and ILC1s.
evidence: Quantification data in Figure 2A shows differential effects on absolute cell numbers.

claim: Expression level of CD49b was slightly upregulated in Prdm1 cko cNK cells and NKp46+ cells in the liver and other tissues.
source: Expression level of CD49b was slightly upregulated in Prdm1 cko cNK cells and NKp46+ cells in the liver and other tissues (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D and E).
evidence: Flow cytometry MFI data shown in supplementary figures demonstrates increased CD49b expression.

claim: Increased CD49a expression was observed in Prdm1 cko liver ILC1s, while it showed decreased expression in NKp46+ cells in the liver, bone marrow, and lymph nodes.
source: Increased CD49a expression was also observed in Prdm1 cko liver ILC1s, while it showed decreased expression in NKp46+ cells in the liver, bone marrow, and lymph nodes (Figure 1—figure supplement 2F and G).
evidence: Flow cytometry MFI data shows differential CD49a expression changes in different cell populations.

claim: Prdm1 is essential for maintaining the balance and homeostasis of cNK cells and ILC1s.
source: These results indicated the essential role of Prdm1 in maintaining the balance and hemostasis of cNK cells and ILC1s.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the observed changes in proportions and numbers of cNK cells and ILC1s.

claim: No significant difference in the in vivo cytotoxicity assay was observed between Prdm1+/+ and Prdm1 cko mice.
source: Although significant impaired homeostasis and maturation of NK cells were observed in Prdm1 cko mice, no significant difference in the in vivo cytotoxicity assay were observed between Prdm1+/+ and Prdm1 cko mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 2H and I).
evidence: B2M-deficient cell rejection assay data shown in supplementary figures shows no difference in direct cytotoxicity.

claim: Deficiency of Prdm1 resulted in more metastasis nodules in both lung (~twofold) and liver (~fourfold) in B16F10 tumor models.
source: Compared with Prdm1+/+ mice, deficiency of Prdm1 resulted in more metastasis nodules in both lung (~twofold) and liver (~fourfold) (Figure 2B and D).
evidence: Tumor metastasis quantification data shown in Figure 2B and D demonstrates increased tumor burden.

claim: Histological analysis confirmed the increased frequency of metastasis tumor foci in Prdm1 cko mice.
source: Histological analysis further confirmed the increased frequency of metastasis tumor foci in Prdm1 cko mice (Figure 2C and E).
evidence: H&E staining images shown in Figure 2C and E provide histological evidence of increased metastasis.

claim: Decreased IFN-γ secretion was observed in Prdm1 cko mice-derived splenic cNK cells, liver cNK cells, and liver ILC1s when stimulated by IL-18 alone or IL-12/IL-18.
source: In agreement with the in vivo data, we also observed decreased IFN-γ secretion in Prdm1 cko mice-derived splenic cNK cells, liver cNK cells, and liver ILC1s when stimulated by IL-18 alone or IL-12/IL-18 (Figure 2F; Figure 2—figure supplement 1; Figure 7—figure supplement 1B), which indicated that Prdm1 is required for full activation of cNK cells and ILC1s in the context of IFN-γ production.
evidence: Flow cytometry data of intracellular IFN-γ staining after cytokine stimulation shown in multiple figures.

claim: Prdm1 is indispensable for NK-cell-mediated tumor surveillance.
source: These data implied that Prdm1 is indispensable for NK-cell-mediated tumor surveillance.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the increased tumor metastasis and decreased IFN-γ production in Prdm1 cko mice.

claim: 445 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified in splenic cNK cells between Prdm1+/+ and Prdm1 cko mice, consisting of 223 upregulated genes and 222 downregulated genes.
source: 445 DEGs were identified out of 17434 protein-coding genes, which consisted of 223 upregulated genes and 222 downregulated genes (Figure 3B).
evidence: Bulk RNA-seq analysis results shown in Figure 3B volcano plot.

claim: Leukocyte-mediated cytotoxicity, immune receptor activity, and integrin binding were enriched in genes that decreased expression in Prdm1 cko mice.
source: In contrast, leukocyte-mediated cytotoxicity, immune receptor activity, and integrin binding were enriched in the genes which decreased their expression level in in Prdm1 cko mice (Figure 3C).
evidence: GO analysis results shown in Figure 3C demonstrate enrichment of specific functional categories.

claim: NF-kappa B signaling pathway enriched in Prdm1-deficient cNK cells.
source: Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) showed that NF-kappa B signaling pathway enriched in Prdm1-deficient cNK cells (Figure 3D), suggesting the potential targets by Prdm1 to regulate NK cell function.
evidence: GSEA results shown in Figure 3D demonstrate pathway enrichment.

claim: Increased expression of multiple transcription factors such as Junb, Batf3, Nfkb1, Tcf7, and Nr4a2 was observed in Prdm1 cko cNK cells.
source: Increased expression of multiple TFs such as Junb, Batf3, Nfkb1, Tcf7, and Nr4a2 was observed in Prdm1 cko cNK cells, suggesting they might be suppressed by Prdm1 (Figure 3E).
evidence: RNA-seq heatmap data shown in Figure 3E demonstrates upregulation of these transcription factors.

claim: Downregulation of granzyme B (Gzmb), Perforin (Prf1) were observed in Prdm1-deficient NK cells.
source: Downregulation of granzyme B (Gzmb), Perforin (Prf1) were observed in Prdm1-deficient NK cells (Figure 3E), implying decreased anti-tumor ability, which was consistent with increased melanoma metastasis in Prdm1 cko mice (Figure 2, B and D).
evidence: RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3E demonstrates decreased expression of cytotoxic molecules.

claim: Decreased expression of Cxcr6 and Cx3cr1 in Prdm1 cko NK cells might be the reason for the increased quantity of NK cells in bone marrow and decreased number in peripheral tissues.
source: CXCR6 and CX3CR1 was considered to play an important role in promoting the egress of NK cells from bone marrow. Decreased expression of Cxcr6 and Cx3cr1 in Prdm1 cko NK (Figure 3E) might be the reason for the increased quantity of NK cells in bone marrow and decreased number in peripheral tissues (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is an inference connecting RNA-seq data with observed NK cell distribution patterns, supported by known roles of these chemokine receptors.

claim: Decreased expression of Il18rap and Il12rb2 were observed in Prdm1 cko cNK cells.
source: Consistent with decreased production of IFN-γ after stimulated by IL-12/IL-18 (Figure 2F), decreased expression of Il18rap and Il12rb2 were observed in Prdm1 cko cNK cells (Figure 3E), implying impaired response to cytokine stimulation.
evidence: RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3E demonstrates decreased expression of cytokine receptor genes.

claim: The percentage of CX3CR1+ cNK cells was significantly decreased in multiple tissues of Prdm1 cko mice.
source: The percentage of CX3CR1+ cNK cells was significantly decreased in multiple tissues of Prdm1 cko mice, while the proportion of CX3CR1+ ILC1 was increased in the liver (Figure 3, F and G).
evidence: Flow cytometry validation data shown in Figure 3F and G confirms RNA-seq findings.

claim: Lower GZMB and PRF1 production was observed in Prdm1-deficient splenic cNK cells, liver cNK cells and ILC1s.
source: Lower GZMB and PRF1 production was observed in Prdm1-deficient splenic cNK cells, liver cNK cells and ILC1s (Figure 3, H-K; Figure 3—figure supplement 1, A-I).
evidence: Flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3 and supplementary figures validates decreased cytotoxic molecule expression.

claim: The proportion of GZMB+ and PRF1+ cNK cells was decreased among almost all of the maturation stages of cNK cells.
source: Notably, the proportion of GZMB+ and PRF1+ cNK cells was decreased among almost all of the maturation stages of cNK cells (Figure 3, J and K).
evidence: Flow cytometry analysis of cytotoxic molecules across maturation stages shown in Figure 3J and K.

claim: Prdm1 may directly influence cytotoxic molecule expression in NK cells, rather than impacting their anti-tumor abilities solely by affecting the maturation phenotype.
source: These findings suggest that Prdm1 may directly influence cytotoxic molecule in NK cells, rather than impacting their anti-tumor abilities solely by affecting the maturation phenotype of Prdm1-deficient NK cells.
evidence: This inference is drawn from the observation that cytotoxic molecules are reduced across all maturation stages.

claim: 10,978 cells passed quality control and were selected for scRNA-seq analysis (6,161 from Prdm1+/+ mice, 4,817 from Prdm1 cko mice).
source: 10,978 cells passed the quality criteria and were selected for further analysis (6,161 from Prdm1+/+ mice, 4,817 from Prdm1 cko mice).
evidence: Quality control metrics for scRNA-seq data are explicitly stated.

claim: Twelve distinct cell clusters were identified from liver CD45+ cells, including B cells, epithelial cells, CD4+ T cells, CD8+ T cells, NKT cells, ILC1s, cNK cells, dendritic cells, monocyte-derived macrophages, Monocytes, Kupffer cells, Neutrophils, and undefined cells.
source: Unsupervised clustering of all sequenced cells based on transcript signatures identified twelve distinct clusters (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), including B cells, epithelial cells (ECs), CD4+ T cells, CD8+ T cells, NKT cells, ILC1s, cNK cells, dendritic cells (DCs), monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs), Monocytes, Kupffer cells (KCs), Neutrophils, and a small number of undefined cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: scRNA-seq clustering results shown in Figure 4A and supplementary figures.

claim: In Prdm1 cko mice, an increased proportion of MDMs, CD4+ T cells, CD8+ T cells, Monocytes, and DCs was observed, alongside a decreased proportion of ECs, cNK cells, ILC1s, and NKT cells.
source: In Prdm1 cko mice, an increased proportion of MDMs, CD4+ T cells, CD8+ T cells, Monocytes, and DCs was observed, alongside a decreased proportion of ECs, cNK cells, ILC1s, and NKT cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: scRNA-seq cell population analysis shown in supplementary figure demonstrates altered immune cell composition.

claim: Both cNK cells and ILC1s have significant reduced proportion in Prdm1 cko mouse liver.
source: Consistent with our flow cytometry data, both cNK cells and ILC1s have significant reduced proportion in Prdm1 cko mouse (Figure 4—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: scRNA-seq data confirms flow cytometry findings regarding reduced group 1 ILC proportions.

claim: In group 1 ILCs from Prdm1 cko mice, there was an increase in the proportion of cNK cells accompanied by a decrease in ILC1s.
source: In group 1 ILCs from Prdm1 cko mice, there was an increase in the proportion of cNK cells accompanied by a decrease in ILC1s (Figure 4, B and C).
evidence: scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 4B and C demonstrates altered cNK/ILC1 ratio.

claim: Liver cNK cells were subdivided into three clusters: 'Prf1 high', 'Junb high', and 'Cxcr3 high' cNK cells.
source: Based on the cluster specific gene expression signature (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A), the subpopulation of liver cNK cells were referred as 'Prf1 high', 'Junb high', and 'Cxcr3 high' cNK cells (Figure 4D), with different distribution in Prdm1 cko and Prdm1+/+ genotype mice (Figure 4F; Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: scRNA-seq subclustering analysis identifies three distinct cNK cell populations based on gene expression.

claim: The Prf1 high cNK cell cluster was defined by high expression of cytolysis-related genes, including Ncr1, Gzma, Gzmb, Prf1, and Fgl2.
source: The Prf1 high cNK cell cluster was defined by high expression of cytolysis-related genes, including Ncr1, Gzma, Gzmb, Prf1, and Fgl2 (Figure 4G; Figure 4—figure supplement 2, C and D), indicating the strong target-killing ability of this cluster.
evidence: Gene expression analysis shown in Figure 4G characterizes the Prf1 high cluster.

claim: There is a significant reduction in Prf1 high cNK cells in Prdm1 cko mice.
source: Although this cluster is present in both Prdm1 cko and Prdm1+/+ mice, there is a significant reduction in Prdm1 cko mice (Figure 4F), indicating the importance of Prdm1 in maintaining this group of cells.
evidence: Cluster proportion analysis shown in Figure 4F demonstrates reduced Prf1 high cNK cells.

claim: GO analysis revealed enrichment of cytolysis, response to virus, and lymphocyte-mediated immunity in genes upregulated in Prf1 high cNK cell cluster.
source: GO analysis further revealed the enrichment signatures of cytolysis, response to virus, and lymphocyte-mediated immunity in the genes upregulated in Prf1 high cNK cell cluster, further confirming the cytotoxic effects of this cluster (Figure 4H).
evidence: GO analysis results shown in Figure 4H characterize functional properties of Prf1 high cluster.

claim: The predominant majority (92.98%) of Junb high liver cNK cells are derived from Prdm1 cko mice.
source: The predominant majority (92.98%) of Junb high liver cNK cells are derived from Prdm1 cko mice, with less than ten percent (7.02%) originating from Prdm1+/+ mice (Figure 4F).
evidence: Cluster composition analysis shown in Figure 4F demonstrates dramatic enrichment of Junb high cells in Prdm1 cko.

claim: Many signal transduction elements and transcription factors, such as Nfkbia, Tnfaip3, Nr4a1/2/3, Batf3, Fos, Fosb, Tcf7, and Kit were upregulated in the Junb high liver cNK cells.
source: Many signal transduction elements, gene expression regulator, and transcriptional factors, such as Nfkbia, Tnfaip3, Nr4a1/2/3, Batf3, Fos, Fosb, Tcf7, and Kit were upregulated in the Junb high liver cNK cells (Figure 4G; Figure 4—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: Gene expression analysis shown in Figure 4G characterizes the Junb high cluster.

claim: The expression of cytotoxicity related genes, such as Gzmb and Prf1, in Junb high cluster was lower than other cNK cell clusters.
source: The expression of cytotoxicity related genes, such as Gzmb and Prf1, in Junb high cluster was lower than other cNK cell clusters (Figure 4G).
evidence: Gene expression comparison shown in Figure 4G demonstrates reduced cytotoxic gene expression in Junb high cluster.

claim: Genes upregulated in Junb high liver cNK cells enriched in cell differentiation, cell activation, and transcriptional regulation.
source: GO analysis showed that genes upregulated in Junb high liver cNK cells enriched in cell differentiation, cell activation, and transcriptional regulation (Figure 4H).
evidence: GO analysis results shown in Figure 4H characterize functional properties of Junb high cluster.

claim: NF-kappa B, IL-17, MAPK, and TNF signaling pathways were upregulated in Junb high cNK cell cluster.
source: GSEA indicates that the NF-kappa B, IL-17, MAPK, and TNF signaling pathways were upregulated in this clusters (Figure 4, I-L).
evidence: GSEA results shown in Figure 4I-L demonstrate pathway enrichment in Junb high cluster.

claim: Mitochondrial related pathways, such as mitochondrial protein, oxidative phosphorylation, and respiratory electron transport chain were suppressed in Junb high cNK cell cluster.
source: GSEA also showed that mitochondrial related pathways, such as mitochondrial protein, oxidative phosphorylation, and respiratory electron transport chain were suppressed in Junb high cNK cell cluster (Figure 4—figure supplement 2, E-G).
evidence: GSEA results shown in supplementary figures demonstrate reduced mitochondrial pathway activity.

claim: Increased proportion of Junb high cluster in Prdm1 deficient cNK cells suggested impaired anti-tumor activity.
source: Increased proportion of Junb high cluster in Prdm1 deficient cNK cells suggested impaired anti-tumor activity, which was consistent with more melanoma metastasis in Prdm1 cko mice and lower expression of cytotoxicity-related genes in splenic cNK cells based on bulk RNA-sequencing.
evidence: This inference connects the increased Junb high cluster with observed tumor phenotypes and gene expression changes.

claim: The Cxcr3 high cNK cell cluster was characterized with high expression of Cxcr3, Ccr2, and some genes encoding ribosomal subunits such as Rps7.
source: The Cxcr3 high cNK cell cluster was characterized with high expression of Cxcr3, Ccr2, and some genes encoding ribosomal subunits such as Rps7 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Gene expression analysis shown in supplementary figure characterizes the Cxcr3 high cluster.

claim: Expression of tissue-resident marker Cd69 was highly expressed in Cxcr3 high cNK cluster.
source: Expression of tissue-resident markers Cd69 was also highly expressed in this clusters (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: Gene expression data shown in supplementary figure demonstrates tissue-resident characteristics.

claim: Cxcr3 high cNK clusters have the highest ILC1 signature score among all cNK clusters.
source: Cxcr3 high cNK clusters have the highest score among all cNK clusters (Figure 4—figure supplement 2H), indicating the similarity with liver ILC1s.
evidence: Module score analysis shown in supplementary figure demonstrates ILC1-like characteristics of Cxcr3 high cluster.

claim: The remarkably decreased proportion of Cxcr3 high cNK cell cluster in Prdm1 cko mice emphasized the critical role of Prdm1 in maintaining this cluster.
source: The remarkably decreased proportion of Cxcr3 high cNK cell cluster in Prdm1 cko mice (Figure 4F) emphasized the critical role of Prdm1 in maintaining this cluster of liver cNK cells, consistent with the flow cytometry result that showed an increase in the number of NK cells in the bone marrow and a decrease in NK cells in peripheral tissues (Figure 1G).
evidence: Cluster proportion analysis connects scRNA-seq findings with flow cytometry observations.

claim: Three clusters of ILC1s were identified: 'Il7r high', 'Klra high', and 'Gzmb high' ILC1s.
source: Three clusters of ILC1s were identified from liver ILC1s (Figure 5A), comprising 'Il7r high', 'Klra high', and 'Gzmb high' ILC1s.
evidence: scRNA-seq subclustering analysis identifies three distinct ILC1 populations.

claim: Prdm1+/+ and Prdm1 cko ILC1s co-cluster largely and have minor difference within the proportion of clusters.
source: Prdm1+/+ and Prdm1 cko ILC1s seemed to co-cluster largely and have minor difference within the proportion of clusters (Figure 5, B and C; Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Cluster analysis shown in Figure 5B and C demonstrates similar ILC1 clustering between genotypes.

claim: Both Gzma and Gzmb expression were downregulated, and Junb was upregulated, in Prdm1 cko mice derived cNK cells and ILC1s compared to those from Prdm1+/+ mice.
source: Additionally, both Gzma and Gzmb expression were downregulated, and Junb was upregulated, in Prdm1 cko mice derived cNK cells and ILC1s compared to those from Prdm1+/+ mice (Figure 5E).
evidence: Ridge plot analysis shown in Figure 5E demonstrates differential gene expression between genotypes.

claim: The Il7r high ILC1s cluster was distinguishable by its high expression of Il7r, Il18r1 (IL18RA), and Ifng (IFN-γ).
source: The Il7r high ILC1s cluster was distinguishable from other ILC1 clusters by its high expression of Il7r, Il18r1 (IL18RA), and Ifng (IFN-γ) (Figure 5B; Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Gene expression analysis characterizes the Il7r high ILC1 cluster.

claim: IL-17, NF-kappa B, TNF, MAPK signaling pathway and T cell differentiation were activated in the Il7r high ILC1 cluster.
source: GSEA and GO analysis showed that IL-17, NF-kappa B, TNF, MAPK signaling pathway and T cell differentiation were activated in the Il7r high ILC1 cluster (Figure 5, F-H; Figure 5—figure supplement 1, E-G).
evidence: GSEA and GO analysis results shown in Figure 5 and supplementary figures characterize pathway activity.

claim: Il7r high ILC1 cluster shows comparable Junb high signature expression pattern with Junb high cNK cell cluster.
source: Module scores, calculated based on the expression of feature genes within the Junb high cNK cell cluster, revealed a comparable Junb high signature expression pattern within the Il7r high ILC1 cluster (Figure 5I).
evidence: Module score analysis shown in Figure 5I demonstrates similarity between Il7r high ILC1 and Junb high cNK clusters.

claim: Several ILC3 signature genes, such as Rora, Tmem176a, and Tmem176b, highly expressed in Il7r high ILC1 cluster.
source: Several ILC3 signature genes, such as Rora, Tmem176a, and Tmem176b (Robinette et al., 2015), highly expressed in this cluster (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Gene expression data shown in supplementary figure demonstrates ILC3-like characteristics with citation to ILC3 signature genes.

claim: Il7r high ILC1 cluster may be attributed to potential plasticity between ILC1 and ILC3 subsets.
source: Considering the close relationship between IL-17-mediated immunity response and ILC3 (Spits et al., 2013; Klose et al., 2013), it is plausible that Il7r high ILC1 cluster may be attributed, at least in part, to potential plasticity between ILC1 and ILC3 subsets.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on observed gene expression patterns and cited literature on ILC plasticity.

claim: There was an elevated proportion of Klra high ILC1s in Prdm1 cko ILC1s (39.7%) compared to Prdm1+/+ ILC1s (28.1%).
source: Notably, there was an elevated proportion of Klra high ILC1s in Prdm1 cko ILC1s (39.7%) compared to Prdm1+/+ ILC1 s (28.1%; Figure 5C).
evidence: Cluster proportion analysis shown in Figure 5C demonstrates increased Klra high ILC1s in Prdm1 cko.

claim: Liver Ly49E+ ILC1s have greater cytotoxic potential and a more robust viral response compared to liver Ly49E- ILC1s.
source: Liver Ly49E+ ILC1s have been identified as possessing greater cytotoxic potential and a more robust viral response compared to liver Ly49E- ILC1s (Chen et al., 2022).
evidence: This is cited knowledge from Chen et al., 2022 about Ly49E+ ILC1 characteristics.

claim: The Klra high cluster exhibited notably high expression of Ccl5.
source: The Klra high cluster exhibited notably high expression of Ccl5 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Gene expression data shown in supplementary figure demonstrates high Ccl5 expression.

claim: CCL5, produced by both cNK cells and ILC1s, plays a pivotal role in facilitating the accumulation of DCs within the tumor microenvironment.
source: Previous research has underscored the pivotal role of CCL5, produced by both cNK cells and ILC1s, in facilitating the accumulation of DCs within the tumor microenvironment, thereby impeding tumor immune evasion, as highlighted in studies (Böttcher et al., 2018; Kirchhammer et al., 2022).
evidence: This is cited knowledge from Böttcher et al., 2018 and Kirchhammer et al., 2022 about CCL5 function.

claim: The expression of Ccl5 was reduced in the Klra high cluster of Prdm1 cko ILC1s compared to Prdm1+/+ ILC1s.
source: The expression of Ccl5 was reduced in the Klra high cluster of Prdm1 cko ILC1s compared to Prdm1+/+ ILC1 s (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D), which could potentially have a detrimental impact on the ability of Klra high ILC1s to develop a connection between innate and adaptive immune responses.
evidence: Gene expression comparison shown in supplementary figure demonstrates reduced Ccl5 in Prdm1 cko.

claim: The proportion of the Gzmb high cluster among liver ILC1s exhibited a considerable reduction in Prdm1 cko mice compared to Prdm1+/+ mice.
source: Consistent with the Prf1 high cNK cell cluster, the proportion of the Gzmb high cluster among liver ILC1s exhibited a considerable reduction in Prdm1 cko mice compared to Prdm1+/+ mice, and the expression of Gzma also downregulated in Prdm1 cko mice (Figure 5B).
evidence: Cluster proportion analysis shown in Figure 5B demonstrates reduced Gzmb high ILC1s.

claim: GzmA+ ILC1 constituted the main population of liver ILC1s at birth, with potential target-killing ability.
source: Previous reports showed that GzmA+ ILC1 constituted the main population of liver ILC1s at birth, with the potential target-killing ability (Di Censo et al., 2021; Friedrich et al., 2021).
evidence: This is cited knowledge from Di Censo et al., 2021 and Friedrich et al., 2021 about GzmA+ ILC1 characteristics.

claim: 17 DEGs are regulated by Prdm1 among liver cNK cells, splenic cNK cells, and liver ILC1s.
source: Through the integration of the bulk RNA-seq and scRNA-seq data, we identified 17 DEGs that are regulated by Prdm1 among liver cNK cells, splenic cNK cells, and liver ILC1s.
evidence: Integration of bulk and single-cell RNA-seq data identifies commonly regulated genes.

claim: Batf3, Junb, Tcf7, and Nfkb1 were upregulated, whereas Gzmb, Prf1, and Fgl2 were downregulated, in both Prdm1 cko liver and splenic cNK cells.
source: Batf3, Junb, Tcf7, and Nfkb1 was upregulated, whereas Gzmb, Prf1, and Fgl2 downregulated, in both Prdm1 cko liver and splenic cNK cells (Figure 5J).
evidence: Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 5J identifies commonly regulated genes across cell types.

claim: Cxcr6 was downregulated in liver ILC1s and splenic cNK cells in Prdm1 cko mice.
source: Cxcr6 was downregulated in liver ILC1s and splenic cNK cells in Prdm1 cko mice (Figure 5J).
evidence: Gene expression analysis shown in Figure 5J demonstrates Cxcr6 downregulation.

claim: A notable negative correlation was observed between the expression levels of Prdm1 and Batf3 in spleen NK cells.
source: Based on the sequencing data published by Flommersfeld et al. (GSE180978), a notable negative correlation was observed between the expression levels of Prdm1 and Batf3 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2I).
evidence: Analysis of published data shown in supplementary figure demonstrates negative correlation.

claim: Prdm1 negatively regulates Batf3 within both spleen and liver NK cells.
source: On top of that, our findings unveiled the negative regulatory influence of Prdm1 on Batf3 within both spleen and liver NK cells.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the observed upregulation of Batf3 in Prdm1 cko cells and negative correlation in published data.

claim: Following the knockout of Hobit, the DEGs were primarily identified within ILC1s, whereas after the knockout of Prdm1, a greater number of DEGs were observed in cNK cells.
source: Following the knockout of Hobit, the DEGs were primarily identified within ILC1s. Conversely, after the knockout of Prdm1, a greater number of DEGs were observed in cNK cells. This indicates that Prdm1 likely possesses a broader range of target genes within cNK cells, whereas Hobit appears to have a more pronounced impact on gene expression within ILC1s (Figure 5—figure supplement 2, C-F).
evidence: Comparative analysis of Prdm1 and Hobit knockout effects shown in supplementary figures.

claim: Genes such as Junb, Fosb, Tcf7, Kit, Gzmb, Prf1, and Cxcr6 were simultaneously upregulated or downregulated in both Prdm1 cko and HobitKO liver cNK cells or ILC1s.
source: Specifically, genes such as Junb, Fosb, Tcf7, Kit, Gzmb, Prf1, and Cxcr6 were simultaneously upregulated or downregulated in both Prdm1 cko and HobitKO liver cNK cells or ILC1s, indicating the similar regulatory networks of Prdm1 and Hobit.
evidence: Comparative analysis identifies overlapping gene regulation between Prdm1 and Hobit.

claim: Following the deletion of Prdm1 in Group 1 ILCs, there is a significant increase in both the proportion and number of macrophages in the liver.
source: Our analysis showed that, following the deletion of Prdm1 in Group 1 ILCs, there is a significant increase in both the proportion and number of macrophages in the liver (Figure 6D).
evidence: Flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6D demonstrates increased liver macrophages.

claim: There is a decrease in the interaction number and interaction strength between liver group 1 ILCs and macrophages (~1.5 fold) in Prdm1 cko mice.
source: Although the quantity of macrophages significantly increases in Prdm1 cko mice, there is a significant decrease in the interaction number and interaction strength between liver group 1 ILCs and macrophages (~1.5 fold) in Prdm1 cko mice (Figure 6, F and G).
evidence: CellChat analysis shown in Figure 6F and G demonstrates reduced cellular interactions.

claim: The reduction of interaction mostly occurred in the cross-talk of ILC1-MDM and ILC1-KC, whereas no difference was observed in cNK-MDM and cNK-KC interaction.
source: The reduction of interaction mostly occurred in the cross-talk of ILC1-MDM and ILC1-KC, whereas no difference was observed in cNK-MDM and cNK-KC interaction (Figure 6—figure supplement 2, A-H).
evidence: Detailed interaction analysis shown in supplementary figures identifies specific interaction changes.

claim: A reduction in the interaction of ligand-receptor, such as Mif-CD74, Cxcl16-Cxcr6, and Cxcl10-Cxcr3 was observed in Prdm1 cko mice compared to Prdm1+/+ mice.
source: A reduction in the interaction of ligand-receptor, such as Mif-CD74, Cxcl16-Cxcr6, and Cxcl10-Cxcr3 was observed in Prdm1 cko mice compared to Prdm1+/+ mice (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Ligand-receptor pair analysis shown in supplementary figure identifies specific reduced interactions.

claim: The information flow of CXCL and MIF pathways significantly decreased in Prdm1 cko mice.
source: Compared to Prdm1+/+ mice, the information flow of CXCL and MIF pathways significantly decreased in Prdm1 cko mice (Figure 6, H and I; Figure 6—figure supplement 2, B, D, F, and H).
evidence: Information flow analysis shown in Figure 6 and supplementary figures demonstrates reduced signaling.

claim: The CXCL signaling was sent from Ly6c2 high Cxcl2 high MDMs and C1q high KC, targeting all ILC1 clusters and Cxcr3 high cNK cell clusters.
source: The CXCL signaling was sent from Ly6c2 high Cxcl2 high MDMs and C1q high KC, targeting all ILC1 clusters and Cxcr3 high cNK cell clusters (Figure 6J).
evidence: Chord plot analysis shown in Figure 6J demonstrates CXCL signaling network.

claim: The impaired CXCL-CXCR interactions might lead to reduced recruitment and activation of group 1 ILCs and macrophages within the tumor microenvironment.
source: The impaired CXCL-CXCR interactions might subsequently lead to reduced recruitment and activation of group 1 ILCs and macrophages within the tumor microenvironment.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the functional consequences of reduced CXCL-CXCR interactions.

claim: A substantial decrease in MFIs of MitoTracker was observed in Prdm1 cko splenic cNK cells, liver cNK cells, and liver ILC1s when compared to their Prdm1+/+ counterparts.
source: A substantial decrease in MFIs of MitoTracker was observed in Prdm1 cko splenic cNK cells, liver cNK cells, and liver ILC1s when compared to their Prdm1+/+ counterparts (Figure 7A).
evidence: Flow cytometry analysis of mitochondrial mass shown in Figure 7A demonstrates reduced mitochondrial content.

claim: There was no significant difference in MitoSOX and TMRM between Prdm1 cko and Prdm1+/+ mice.
source: There was no significant difference in MitoSOX and TMRM between Prdm1 cko and Prdm1+/+ mice (Figure 7, B and C), which suggested that the ATP synthesize capacity was minimally affected by Prdm1.
evidence: Flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 7B and C demonstrates no change in mitochondrial ROS or membrane potential.

claim: The number of both cNK cells and ILC1s have significant decreased in tumor-bearing liver of Prdm1 cko mice.
source: The proportion changes of cNK cells and ILC1s in Prdm1 cko mice was similar with the no tumor-burden condition, while the number of both cNK cells and ILC1s have significant decreased in tumor-bearing liver (Figure 7D).
evidence: Flow cytometry analysis of tumor-bearing mice shown in Figure 7D demonstrates reduced group 1 ILC numbers.

claim: Significant decrease of IFN-γ+ cells were observed in Prdm1 cko mice liver cNK cells and ILC1s under the combined stimulation of IL-12/IL-18 in tumor-bearing mice.
source: Compared with Prdm1+/+ mice, significant deceased of IFN-γ+ cells were observed in Prdm1 cko mice liver cNK cells and ILC1s under the combinate stimulation of IL-12/IL-18 (Figure 7E; Figure 7—figure supplement 1B), which was more remarkable in liver ILC1s.
evidence: Flow cytometry analysis of IFN-γ production in tumor-bearing mice shown in Figure 7E demonstrates impaired cytokine production.

claim: Group 1 innate lymphoid cells comprise conventional natural killer (cNK) cells and type 1 innate lymphoid cells (ILC1s).
source: Group 1 innate lymphoid cells (ILCs) comprise conventional natural killer (cNK) cells and type 1 innate lymphoid cells (ILC1s).
evidence: This is a definitional statement establishing the composition of Group 1 ILCs.

claim: The main functions of liver cNK cells and ILC1s include directly killing target cells and regulating local immune microenvironment through cytokine secretion.
source: The main functions of liver cNK cells and ILC1s not only include directly killing target cells but also regulating local immune microenvironment of the liver through the secretion of cytokines.
evidence: This is a summary statement of established functions of liver group 1 ILCs.

claim: Prdm1 maintains functional subsets of cNK cells and liver ILC1s.
source: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data also provided evidences that Prdm1 maintains functional subsets of cNK cells and liver ILC1s and facilitates communications between cNK cells, liver ILC1s, and macrophages.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from scRNA-seq analysis presented in the study.

claim: Prdm1 facilitates communications between cNK cells, liver ILC1s, and macrophages.
source: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data also provided evidences that Prdm1 maintains functional subsets of cNK cells and liver ILC1s and facilitates communications between cNK cells, liver ILC1s, and macrophages.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from CellChat analysis of scRNA-seq data.
